Description

Mast cells release arachidonic acid from membrane phospholipids through cytosolic phospholipase A2 and make mainly prostaglandin D2 and leukotriene C4. Cyclooxygenases 1 and 2 turn arachidonic acid into PGG2 and then PGH2, from which specific synthases and reductases make PGE2, PGD2, PGF2alpha, PGI2 and thromboxane A2. The lipoxygenases ALOX5, ALOX12 and ALOX15 make the hydroperoxy and hydroxy acids, the leukotrienes LTB4 and LTC4 to LTE4, lipoxins, eoxins and hepoxilins. Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and paracetamol inhibit the cyclooxygenase reaction, and corticosteroids reduce the release of arachidonic acid. PGE2, PGI2 and LTB4 leave the cell and act on the receptors of the nociceptor, PGE2 through the exporter ABCC4.

Colour

Red raises pain, blue relieves it, and olive is shared signalling whose effect is set by the receptor upstream. Drugs are yellow and classes of molecules white. Enzymes take the colour of what they make or remove. Each molecule is coloured by its role in this block.

Red are the prostaglandins E2, I2 and F2alpha, the HpETEs and HETEs, the hepoxilins and the leukotrienes, which sensitise nociceptors or drive inflammation, and the enzymes that make them. Blue are the lipoxins and 15-epi-lipoxins, which stop neutrophil infiltration and attenuate inflammatory pain (Svensson 2007), and the enzymes that inactivate red mediators. Olive are the intermediates, the inactive products and the molecules acting both ways (PGD2, 12-HHT, ALOX15).
